1.en: Whoever strives shall find, and whoever sows shall reap.

2.en: Resolve comes in the measure of those who hold it, and noble deeds in the measure of the noble.

3.en: If you venture after a lofty honor, settle for nothing less than the stars.

4.en: Whoever fears to climb the mountains will live forever among the pits.

5.en: Goals are not won by wishing; the world is taken by striving.

6.en: Heights are gained in the measure of toil; whoever seeks the summit must keep the night awake.

7.en: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.

8.en: It does not matter how slowly you go, as long as you do not stop.

9.en: If you can't fly, then run; if you can't run, then walk; if you can't walk, then crawl; but whatever you do, you have to keep moving forward.

10.en: You don't have to be great to start, but you have to start to be great.

11.en: Do what you can, with what you have, where you are.

12.en: Whether you think you can, or you think you can't, you're right.

13.en: The way to get started is to quit talking and begin doing.

14.en: Be the change you wish to see in the world.

15.en: Whatever the mind can conceive and believe, it can achieve.

16.en: Fear does not prevent death; it prevents life.

17.en: If you add nothing to the world, you are yourself a surplus to it.

18.en: Nothing scratches your skin like your own nail, so take charge of all your affairs yourself.
18.note_en: Rely on yourself, for no one tends to your needs as well as you do.

20.en: Every diligent person has a share.

21.en: Do not put off today's work until tomorrow.

22.en: The mind is the mightiest weapon.

23.en: Success is the sum of small efforts, repeated day in and day out.

24.en: The only way to do great work is to love what you do.

25.en: I have not failed; I've just found ten thousand ways that won't work.

26.en: Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.

27.en: It always seems impossible until it's done.

28.en: Discipline is the bridge between goals and accomplishment.

29.en: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.

30.en: Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.

31.en: It takes twenty years to build a reputation and five minutes to ruin it.

33.en: Learn more from failure than you learn from success.

34.en: Time is like a sword: if you do not cut it, it will cut you.
34.note_en: Use your time well, or it will be lost to your cost.

35.en: In patience lies safety, and in haste lies regret.

36.en: The first of the rain is a single drop.
36.note_en: Great things grow from small beginnings.

37.en: People don't buy what you do; they buy why you do it.

38.en: Not all that a man desires does he attain; the winds blow as the ships would not wish.

39.en: Let the days do as they will, and be at peace when fate decrees.

40.en: Nations live only as long as their morals endure; when their morals are gone, they are gone.

41.en: Be beautiful, and you will see the world as beautiful.

42.en: Each person's worth lies in what they do well.
42.author_en: Attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib

43.en: The vanquished are forever eager to imitate the victor.

44.en: Your children are not your children. They are the sons and daughters of Life's longing for itself.

45.en: The unexamined life is not worth living.

46.en: Life is like riding a bicycle: to keep your balance, you must keep moving.

47.en: Yesterday I was clever, so I wanted to change the world. Today I am wise, so I am changing myself.

48.en: Nothing is more powerful than an idea whose time has come.

49.en: The best speech is brief and to the point.

50.en: If speech is silver, then silence is golden.

51.en: An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.

52.en: Many a harm brings hidden good.
52.note_en: Misfortune can turn out to be a blessing in disguise.

53.en: A sound mind in a sound body.

54.en: If you are not part of the solution, you are part of the problem.

55.en: Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much.

56.en: The noblest place on earth is the saddle of a swift horse, and the best companion in any age is a book.

57.en: Rise for the teacher and give him full honor; the teacher is almost a messenger.

58.en: Education, like water and air, is the right of every human being.

59.en: Imagination is more important than knowledge.

60.en: Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.

61.en: Education is the passport to the future, for tomorrow belongs to those who prepare for it today.

62.en: If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.

63.en: Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood. Now is the time to understand more, so that we may fear less.

64.en: An investment in knowledge pays the best interest.

65.en: The roots of education are bitter, but the fruit is sweet.

66.en: A little knowledge that acts is worth infinitely more than much knowledge that is idle.

67.en: Learning in youth is like carving in stone.
67.note_en: What is learned when young stays for life.

68.en: Seek knowledge from the cradle to the grave.

69.en: I soothe my soul with hopes I watch for; how narrow life would be, were it not for the wide space of hope.

70.en: It grew tight, and when its rings closed fast, it opened, though I thought it never would.

71.en: If, one day, a people wills to live, then fate must surely answer.

72.en: Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement.

73.en: Patience is the key to relief.

74.en: Tighten, O hardship, and you will break open.
74.note_en: When a crisis reaches its worst, relief is near.

75.en: After hardship comes ease, and after the night rises the dawn.

76.en: Every sunrise gives you a new chance to begin again.

77.en: A leader is one who knows the way, goes the way, and shows the way.

78.en: Management is doing things right; leadership is doing the right things.

79.en: There is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all.

80.en: Innovation distinguishes between a leader and a follower.

81.en: The master of a people is their servant.
81.note_en: True leadership means serving those you lead.

82.en: The most dangerous phrase in the language is: We've always done it this way.

83.en: The best way to predict the future is to invent it.

84.en: Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.

85.en: The most profound technologies are those that disappear; they weave themselves into the fabric of everyday life until they are indistinguishable from it.

86.en: Talk is cheap. Show me the code.

87.en: Simplicity is a prerequisite for reliability.

88.en: Your most unhappy customers are your greatest source of learning.

90.en: Technology is a tool; it is people who give it meaning.

92.en: AI is one of the most profound things we're working on as humanity, more profound than fire or electricity.

93.en: Our success in creating AI could be the biggest event in the history of our civilization, or the worst.

94.en: There is nothing artificial about AI. It is inspired by people, created by people, and, most importantly, it impacts people.

95.en: The question of whether machines can think is no more interesting than the question of whether submarines can swim.

96.en: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.

97.en: AI will not replace you, but someone who masters it might.

99.en: The media is the most powerful entity on earth. It has the power to make the innocent guilty and the guilty innocent.

100.en: The media either builds awareness or washes it away.

101.en: The media is the instrument of a society's awareness.

102.en: Verify before you share, for every word is a trust.

103.en: The one standing on the shore is always a fine swimmer.
103.note_en: It is easy to judge and advise when you are not the one facing the hardship.

104.en: The camel never sees the crook in its own neck.
104.note_en: People notice others' faults but are blind to their own.

105.en: Hand joined to hand throws far.
105.note_en: Together people achieve what no one can achieve alone.

106.en: The pen does not cure dullness.
106.note_en: Schooling alone cannot give a person good sense.

107.en: Lose a third of your wealth rather than all of it.
107.note_en: Accept a partial loss to save yourself from total ruin.

108.en: Mourning is led by the family of the departed.
108.note_en: Those a matter concerns most must care for it most and take the lead.

109.en: A shameful deed is always disowned.
109.note_en: No one willingly admits to a disgraceful act.

110.en: Do not hand the ladle to one who does not know how to serve.
110.note_en: Entrust a task only to someone capable of doing it.

111.note_en: Recovery and improvement come gradually, so be patient.

112.en: What the goat does to the qarad tree, she will find on her own hide.
112.note_en: The goat eats the qarad pods that are later used to tan her skin: what you do comes back to you.

113.en: Drag the thorns across a hide that is not your own.
113.note_en: People are careless with what does not belong to them and do not feel another's pain.

114.en: A letter's address tells you enough of its contents.
114.note_en: First signs are often enough to reveal the whole matter.

115.en: In his mother's eyes, the monkey is a gazelle.

116.en: Though I come last in time, I shall bring what the ancients could not.

117.en: No goal stays out of reach for a people whose steed is daring.

118.en: Were it not for hardship, all men would be lords: generosity brings poverty, and daring brings death.

119.en: Fear is only what a man chooses to fear, and safety only what he deems safe.

120.en: Be patient and you will attain.

122.en: What cannot be attained in full should not be abandoned in full.

123.en: Better to arrive late than never to arrive.

124.note_en: Action and effort bring reward, while idleness brings nothing.

125.en: Knowing is not enough; we must apply. Willing is not enough; we must do.

126.en: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.

127.en: The man who moves a mountain begins by carrying away small stones.

128.en: Anyone who has never made a mistake has never tried anything new.

129.en: You don't have to see the whole staircase, just take the first step.

130.en: Every morning is a blank page, so write on it something worth reading.

131.en: Do not wait for perfect conditions; begin with what is in your hands, and the road will widen.

132.en: Dreams do not come true by sleeping, but by waking up for them every day.

133.en: Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life.

134.en: You can't connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backward.

135.en: The most important investment you can make is in yourself.

136.en: We always overestimate the change that will occur in the next two years and underestimate the change that will occur in the next ten.

137.en: One never notices what has been done; one can only see what remains to be done.

138.en: Every steed may stumble, and every scholar may err.

140.en: Every delay holds some hidden good.

141.en: No right is ever lost while someone still demands it.

142.en: A little that lasts is better than much that ceases.

143.en: Success is not a station you reach, but a way you travel.

144.en: Failure is not the opposite of success, but part of it.

145.en: The days will reveal to you what you did not know, and news will come to you from one you never sent to seek it.

146.en: Whatever trait a man may hold, though he thinks it hidden from people, it will become known.

147.en: A man's tongue is half of him, his heart the other half; what remains is but a form of flesh and blood.

148.en: We blame our times, yet the fault lies within us; our times have no fault but us.

149.en: When the fool speaks, do not answer him; silence is better than a reply.

150.en: The eye of approval is blind to every fault, but the eye of resentment lays every flaw bare.

151.en: When you see the lion's fangs bared, do not think the lion is smiling.

152.en: One whose mouth is bitter with sickness finds even pure, sweet water bitter.

153.en: The man of reason suffers amid bliss because of his mind, while the ignorant one lives in bliss amid misery.

154.en: People are enemies of what they do not know.
154.author_en: Attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib

155.en: May God have mercy on the one who shows me my faults as a gift.

156.en: It is not things that disturb people, but their judgments about them.

157.en: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.

158.en: He who knows others is clever; he who knows himself is wise.

159.en: Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one thinks of changing himself.

161.en: All that glitters is not gold.

162.en: Once the cause is known, the wonder fades.

163.en: Every vessel seeps with what it holds.
163.note_en: A person's words and deeds reveal what lies within them.

164.en: Ask one who has experienced, not one who is merely wise.
164.note_en: Practical experience is a better guide than theory.

165.en: Necessity is the mother of invention.

166.en: A sparrow in the hand is better than ten on the tree.

167.en: What one grows up on, one grows old on.
167.note_en: Habits formed in youth stay with a person for life.

168.en: Every occasion has its fitting words.

169.en: The sword has outrun the reproach.
169.note_en: The deed is already done, and blame now comes too late.

170.note_en: Said of one whose own actions cause their downfall.

171.en: Tomorrow is near for the one who watches for it.
171.note_en: What is awaited will soon come and reveal the truth.

172.en: The eye sees far, but the hand is short.
172.note_en: One can see what one wants but lacks the means to reach it.

173.en: The people of Mecca know its mountain paths best.
173.note_en: Those who live with a matter understand it best.

174.en: The best of matters is the middle way.

175.en: No one who seeks counsel comes to regret.

176.en: A day for you, and a day against you.

177.en: They planted and we ate; we plant so that others may eat.

178.en: A book is read from its title.
178.note_en: The outward signs of a thing reveal much about its substance.

179.en: When a thing exceeds its limit, it turns into its opposite.

181.en: Injustice heralds the ruin of civilization.

182.en: Ignorance leads to fear, fear leads to hatred, and hatred leads to violence.

183.en: I am the sea, with pearls hidden in its depths; have they asked the diver about my shells?

184.en: Leave your homeland in pursuit of greatness, and travel, for in travel lie five benefits.

185.en: Whoever studies the books of science, if his aim is to know the truth, must make himself an adversary of everything he reads.

186.en: Knowledge is light, and ignorance is darkness.

187.en: The bane of knowledge is forgetting.

188.en: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.

189.en: Science is more a way of thinking than a body of knowledge.

190.en: He who learns but does not think is lost; he who thinks but does not learn is in danger.

191.en: Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body.

192.en: Every book you read is a new window through which you look out on the world.

193.en: A good question is half of knowledge.

194.en: On this earth there is what makes life worth living.

195.en: Even the darkest night will end, and the sun will rise.

196.en: Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only love can do that.

197.en: Everything can be taken from a man but one thing: the freedom to choose his attitude in any given set of circumstances.

198.en: I learned that courage was not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it.

199.en: He said: The sky is gloomy, and he frowned. I said: Smile; the gloom in the sky is enough.

200.en: Many a calamity leaves a man at his wits' end, yet with God lies the way out.

201.en: After the clouds, the sun shines.

202.en: However long the night, the dawn must come.

203.en: A seed does not see the sun in its first days, yet it grows toward it.

204.en: Hardship tightens only so that it may give way to relief.
204.note_en: When things are at their hardest, relief is near.

205.en: A leader is best when people barely know he exists; when his work is done, they will say: we did it ourselves.

206.en: Leadership is the art of getting someone else to do something you want done because he wants to do it.

207.en: Lead from the back, and let others believe they are in front.

208.en: Sound judgment comes before the courage of the brave; it comes first, and courage takes second place.

209.en: Choose the companion before the road.
209.note_en: Pick your company carefully before setting out on any journey or venture.

212.en: A true leader makes leaders, not followers.

213.en: Any fool can write code that a computer can understand. Good programmers write code that humans can understand.

214.en: Premature optimization is the root of all evil in programming.

215.en: Make it work, make it right, make it fast.

216.en: The Analytical Engine weaves algebraic patterns just as the loom weaves flowers and leaves.

218.en: Technology that does not serve people becomes a burden on them.

219.en: If a typical person can do a mental task with less than one second of thought, we can probably automate it using AI either now or in the near future.

220.en: As soon as it works, no one calls it AI anymore.

221.en: A good question to AI is half the answer.

222.en: The machine memorizes, and the human understands; so be the one who understands.

223.en: If liberty means anything at all, it means the right to tell people what they do not want to hear.

224.en: The bane of news is those who relay it.
224.note_en: News is distorted most by the people who pass it on.

225.en: A lie flies, while the truth walks on foot.

226.en: Not all that is known should be said, and not all that is said has found its time.

227.en: A friend in need is a friend indeed.

228.en: Tell me who your companions are, and I will tell you who you are.

229.en: Many a brother of yours was not born of your mother.
229.note_en: A true friend can be as close as a blood brother.

230.en: Choose the neighbor before the house.
230.note_en: A good neighbor matters more than the home itself.

231.en: Solitude is better than bad company.

232.en: Out of sight, out of mind.

233.en: Farewell to the world if it holds no true friend, faithful to his word and fair.

234.en: If a man cares for you only out of obligation, let him go, and do not grieve over him too much.

235.en: A friend is a single soul dwelling in two bodies.

236.en: I would rather walk with a friend in the dark than alone in the light.

237.en: A true friend sees the pain in your eyes while others believe your smile.

238.en: No nation's edifice stands firm when its morals lie in ruins.

239.en: The soundness of your affairs rests on character; so set your soul right by virtue, and you will stand upright.

240.en: Honor the noble and you win him over; honor the base and he grows insolent.

241.en: Injustice from one's own kin cuts deeper than the blow of a sharp Indian sword.

242.en: Since when have you enslaved people when their mothers bore them free?

243.en: Do not be the slave of another when God has made you free.
243.author_en: Attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib

244.en: If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.

245.en: The weak can never forgive; forgiveness is the attribute of the strong.

246.en: Your tongue is your steed: guard it and it guards you; betray it and it betrays you.

247.en: Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it.

248.en: As you judge, so shall you be judged.

249.en: Whoever feels safe from punishment forgets his manners.

250.en: Generosity comes from what one has.
250.note_en: Give within your means; no one is expected to give what they do not have.

251.en: It is when you give of yourself that you truly give.

252.en: Character is measured not by what you say, but by what you do when no one is watching.

253.en: Contentment is a treasure that never runs out.

254.en: Whoever watches people dies of worry.
254.note_en: Constantly comparing yourself to others or fretting over their opinions only brings misery.

255.en: O you who complain while nothing ails you, how will you be when real illness comes?

256.en: One whose soul holds no beauty sees nothing beautiful in all existence.

257.en: Our life is what our thoughts make it.

259.en: Happiness is not something ready-made; it comes from your own actions.

260.en: The best and most beautiful things in the world cannot be seen or even touched; they must be felt with the heart.

261.en: Wealth consists not in having great possessions, but in having few wants.

262.en: Happiness is rejoicing in what you have, not grieving over what you lack.

263.en: Your smile to the morning is the first gift you give yourself.

264.en: The beats of a man's heart keep telling him: life is but minutes and seconds.

265.en: O son of Adam, you are nothing but days; whenever a day passes, a part of you is gone.

266.en: It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a great deal of it.

268.en: Time is breaths that never return.

269.en: Work in silence, and let your success make the noise.

270.en: An hour of planning saves you days of toil.

271.en: The early morning carries the blessing of the whole day.

272.en: A mother is a school: prepare her well, and you prepare a people of noble roots.

273.en: All that I am, or hope to be, I owe to my mother.

274.en: A home is not walls, but the hearts that dwell within it.

275.en: Honoring your parents is a debt you repay to them, and a loan your children will repay to you.

276.en: Family is where life begins and love never ends.
